 SOUTH CAROLINA (WPDE) — South Carolina SNAP recipients can no longer use their benefits to purchase certain candy and sugary drinks under new restrictions that took effect November 1, 2026.
 The changes are part of the state’s Healthy Food SC initiative, which removes candy, energy drinks, soft drinks and other sweetened beverages from the list of items eligible for purchase through the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP).
 Recipients can still purchase these items, but they will have to pay for them using money outside their SNAP benefits.
 Gov. Henry McMaster said the goal of the restrictions is to encourage healthier food choices.
 “By encouraging families to purchase healthy, nutritious food – and not junk food – we ensure federal taxpayer dollars are used to their maximum benefit and keep South Carolina at the forefront of the effort to Make America Healthy Again - South Carolina Governor, Henry McMaster While many sweets are no longer eligible, several products will still qualify under SNAP benefits, including:
 Bakery products such as cookies, brownies and muffins.
 Diet and zero-sugar soft drinks.
 Granola and protein bars.
 Baking ingredients such as chocolate chips, melting wafers, toffee bits and sprinkles.
 Beverages containing milk or milk substitutes.
 The restrictions apply to all SNAP-authorized retailers in South Carolina. Recipients cannot opt out of the changes.
 The new rules do not change who qualifies for SNAP assistance or the amount of benefits recipients receive.
 The state plans to survey SNAP recipients and retailers about the changes in early December.
